title: Weekly Park Visits Linked to Children's Wellbeing
paragraphs: Many parents ask if parks are good for children. A new study from the Universities of Exeter and Bristol says that weekly park visits may help.

The team used information from a long study called Children of the 90s. It followed 4,219 children between the ages of 4 and 11. Children who went to a park at least once a week from birth to age 11 scored, on average, 16.5 percent better in mental health tests than children who went less often.
The scientists also looked at family problems and money, and the results stayed the same. But this kind of study can only show a link. It cannot prove that parks cause better mental health.

questions.q: How much better did weekly park visitors score?
Can the study prove parks cause better mental health?
questions.a: No, it can only show a link.
